subject: POC Trial Environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap & next steps 1 environment selection (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Hi Sam 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 3-week POC so we can align on success criteria and environment: 

Success criteria (what you called out):
- End-to-end latency under 300ms for 95th percentile on your 1k token use case.
- Cost target: <= $0.015 per 1k tokens for inference (target goal to compare across configs).
- Integration: embeddings + chat generation with our SDK and a sample of your telemetry events flowing through the prefix cache.
- Security: SOC2 controls verified and optional VPC if you require private networking.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize environment choice (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial), provide access and network requirements.
- Week 1: ingest sample data, run baseline tests (latency/cost), iterate prompts.
- Week 2: run production-like load tests and measure P95, caching impact, and cost.
- Week 3: deliver final report + recommendation and handoff.

Ownership / roles:
- Marissa (me): program owner, timelines, customer success coordination.
- Dev Patel (cc): technical lead for environment setup and network onboarding.
- Your team: Sam (POC sponsor) and Jordan (tech lead) for acceptance tests.

Questions we have to confirm:
1) Which environment do you prefer to start in? Our hosted sandbox is fastest to stand up; Dedicated sandbox gives isolated GPUs and predictable throughput; VPC trial gives private networking and KMS options but requires network coordination.
2) Who on your side will own firewall/VPN and can provide a point of contact for VPC peering or IP allowlist?
3) Any specific compliance (KMS/HSM, data residency) we should plan for during the trial?

Attached: poc-checklist.pdf (high level tasks) and network-reqs.xlsx (IP ranges, ports, SSO/KMS notes). I've also attached the dedicated pricing overview for reference.

Proposed next steps: please reply with chosen environment and contact for networking by EOD Friday. We'll then schedule a 30-min tech kickoff with Dev.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC recap & next steps 1 environment selection (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Thanks Marissa 

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers from our side:
- Success criteria: agree with the list you put together. Add one more: model output stability (no more than 5% regression vs our baseline prompts).
- Environment: we'd like to start in a Dedicated sandbox (isolated pool) to get realistic throughput numbers; if the VPC option is low friction we'd prefer that but we can start dedicated and switch to VPC week 2 if needed.
- Timeline: 3-week POC works. Target start next Monday if that's possible.
- Network contact: Jordan Ellis (cc) will coordinate with our network engineer  Jordan, can you share an internal contact for firewall/peering and any maintenance windows?

Also looping in procurement for a short statement of work and to confirm billing approach.

Sam Reynolds
Head of Product, Acme Analytics
sam.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC recap & next steps 1 environment selection (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Great  thanks for confirming, Sam.

Plan: we'll provision a Dedicated sandbox cluster Monday AM and keep the VPC option open. Dev, can you start the provisioning flow and mark any blockers for Jordan's team?

Jordan  attaching network-reqs.xlsx with the IP ranges and ports we need for dedicated sandbox peering. For an initial sandbox we generally need a static egress IP allowlist and optional VPC peering for private traffic. If you're able to share a network contact and a preferred maintenance window (weekend nights are usually easiest), we'll schedule the peering work.

I've also attached the dedicated pricing overview so procurement has context. If procurement needs an SOW we can draft one this week.

Next: Tech kickoff Monday 10am PT  30 minutes. Invite incoming.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: poc-checklist.pdf, network-reqs.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC provisioning questions

On it  quick technical notes before the kickoff:
- For dedicated sandbox we'll provision a 4x A10G GPU pool to match expected load; we'll tune batch sizes after first load test.
- VPC peering: we support both IP allowlist and VPC peering. Peering requires routing and a security review from Acme netops (Jordan's team).
- KMS: if you want encrypted keys in your KMS, we'll need the key ARN and an IAM role for access.
- Sample data ingest: please provide a 1-2k example dataset (anonymized) so we can prewarm caches.

I'll post a short checklist in the kickoff invite.

 Dev
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
